events.title: Armistice Ends World War I
events.description: At 11:00 a.m. Germany and the Allied powers signed an armistice in a railway carriage at Compiègne, France, ending fighting on the Western Front after more than four years of war.
events.significance: The ceasefire brought an end to World War I combat, which had killed millions. The date is commemorated as Armistice Day, Remembrance Day, and Veterans Day in many countries.

events.title: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier Dedicated at Arlington
events.description: President Warren G. Harding presided over the burial of an unidentified American soldier killed in World War I at Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia.
events.significance: The tomb became a national symbol of sacrifice and honor for all service members who died without being identified, and it remains guarded around the clock.

events.title: Angola Declares Independence from Portugal
events.description: Angola proclaimed independence after nearly five centuries of Portuguese rule, with Agostinho Neto becoming the first president under the MPLA as rival movements competed for control.
events.significance: Independence was followed by a long civil war involving Cold War powers that lasted until 2002 and shaped the modern history of southern Africa.

events.title: Rhodesia Issues Unilateral Declaration of Independence
events.description: Prime Minister Ian Smith's white-minority government declared Rhodesia independent from Britain to avoid transition to majority rule.
events.significance: The declaration was condemned internationally, led to United Nations sanctions, and helped spark a guerrilla war that ended with the creation of Zimbabwe in 1980.

events.title: Birth of Fyodor Dostoevsky
events.description: Russian novelist Fyodor Dostoevsky was born in Moscow. He later wrote works including Crime and Punishment, The Idiot, and The Brothers Karamazov.
events.significance: Dostoevsky's psychological and philosophical novels profoundly influenced world literature, existentialism, and modern psychology.
